newsitem.title: POLAND: Merrill sees fast start, dull Q1 for Polish bourse.
newsitem.headline: Merrill sees fast start, dull Q1 for Polish bourse.

text.p: The Polish bourse should see a dull first quarter after a quick start, with large flotations making the whole year look bright, Merrill Lynch said in its January European Emerging Markets Strategy Report.

"Interest rates appear unlikely to fall in the short term with consumption levels worrying the central bank. As such we expect that the first quarter will be dull following an initial period of fresh investment," the report said.
The Warsaw bourse's main market has risen 11.4 percent so far this year.

Merrill said a good sign for the bourse in 1997 was the flotation of shares in the 15 National Investment Funds (NFIs) in the country's mass privatisation scheme and the flotations of copper firm KGHM Polska Miedz SA and Bank Handlowy SA.
"As such the Polish capital market could conceivably double in size, bringing greater liquidity and facilitating further key privatisations," the report said.
It said a pick-up in economic growth in Europe as a whole and Russia could help exporters such as Agros, Debica, Irena, Jutrzenka, Swarzedz, as well as the cable sector.

Merrill placed BIG among its top European emerging market picks, maintaining its accumulate rating and saying the stock was trading at too large a discount -- 30-40 percent -- to banks Slaski and BRE.
